note: Routes that cannot be driven by any gauntlet tier today. Every entry names WHY and WHO. A route with no entry and no observation appears in the report's 'NO stated reason at all' row, which is the row that should make someone uncomfortable. 'No tier drives it yet' is a real and admissible reason; it is deliberately NOT phrased as 'blocked' when nothing structural prevents it, so that a missing test never launders itself into an external blocker. Rules: most specific matching rule wins; a trailing '*' is a prefix glob; keep an entry only while it is true, and delete it the moment its route executes. Every entry also carries a `class`, and tools/genref/generate.mjs refuses this file if one is missing or unknown, because the register's honest never-executed figure is a sum over two of these classes. out-of-release-set: no tier deploys the program at all. structural: genuinely undrivable at HEAD, and the entry argues why. repointing: not a block -- the entry redirects a reader, or records one already discharged. unwired: the route IS driven today and emits no census evidence, which is a wiring defect and not a protocol one. status-report: no campaign or tier drives it yet, and nothing structural is in the way. The last two are the classes that count as never-executed however carefully they are worded, because a sentence in this file is not an execution.

Driven today by programs/dclutch-accelerator-sbf/dealer-program-test (12,062 lines, the accepted/frontier/physical suites over the real ELF), which emits no census evidence and has no bindings, so the two set_return_data arms read as never executed. The accelerator ELF itself is deployed and Registry-pinned beside the seven roles (general_accelerator.* in the cohort manifest), so the old out-of-release-set reason no longer holds for this arm; what is missing is evidence wiring and a runner, exactly the dealer-checkpoint shape. Cohort-17's scoring Dealer replaces the selector-9 evaluation this arm hosts (MECHANISM_SCORING_DEALER section 2, section 6). Previous entry, kept for its history: Dealer accelerator, not part of the seven-role successor release set; no tier deploys it. THE FRAME-CLEANLINESS HALF OF THIS ROW IS RESOLVED (W2h, 2026-08-27): measured at c3c4950 and again at 5e25f8e, cargo build-sbf on programs/dclutch-dealer-accelerator-sbf emits ZERO 'overwrites values in the frame' diagnostics, against 253 measured on the same tree at the immediately preceding HEAD. TA-DLR's root cause was correct and is independent of the fix: with `no-entrypoint` set, dclutch-trading-sbf compiles without its own #[global_allocator], which leaves __rust_alloc an opaque extern that cannot be folded at its call sites and spills hot_v3::process_hot_execution_v3 past the SBPF v0 4,096-byte frame. What changed is the headroom, not the allocator: process_hot_execution_v3 used 3,904 bytes of that frame with the outgoing-argument area filling the rest, and c3c4950 split it into an authentication half (3,008 bytes) and an execution half (2,496), which absorbs the opaque extern. TA-DLR's two-edit patch is therefore NOT required for this row and is NOT applied. It remains the principled fix for the underlying incoherence -- a no-entrypoint library build of Trading still runs Hot code under whichever allocator its host executable installs, not the one the shipped Trading program uses -- and if it is taken: re-measure on top of c3c4950 rather than against the stale 253; land both halves together (either alone is a duplicate or a missing #[global_allocator], both hard errors); and per W1f keep admit_heap_frame_v1 and lift_declared_heap_profile_v1 reachable in the SHIPPED ELF, where DCLTPCB1 depends on them on chain now. Widening the cfg does not move the shipped build either way, since `no-entrypoint` is off there and both predicates already evaluate the same. The emitted accelerator .so was never contaminated in any case: process_hot_execution_v3 is dead-stripped from it.

THE FIX IS ONE FIELD AND IT BELONGS TO `market.rs`'s OWNER, not to this arm: `LocalMarketShapeV1` needs a caller-stated primary shelf life (default `None` = the fixture's own, so every existing caller compiles byte-identically), threaded into `max_age_seconds` and into `authored_relative_ladder_v1`'s anchor, plus a `--terminal-max-age-seconds` flag on the loopback market command. That is the honest alternative to warping a validator's clock, and it is no more of a lab setting than the constant it replaces: a frozen publication's staleness grows by 86,400 every day and is a fact about the LAB. MEASURED UNDER EXACTLY THAT PATCH on 2026-09-04, in a private worktree, on one loopback validator: the route executes twice. The primary leg was due at 1788572039 and the crank landed at 1788572040 -- ONE SECOND after, which is the strictness itself -- writing RecoveryAdvanced for 204,690 CU over an 18-account frame, and the Source read back phase Recovery attempt 0. The rung's own committed deadline was 1788572159 and the second crank landed at 1788572160 for 197,216 CU, and the Source read back Exhausted. For comparison the real-ELF program-test figures are advance 216,637 / exhaust 218,163; these are single loopback draws with fresh keypairs and bump-search noise in them. One `max_age` governs both the crank's admissibility and the publication's freshness, so a shelf life short enough for the primary leg to close inside a lab run is one under which the frozen publication is already stale for every rung after it. A rung answered on a loopback needs a publication the lab can refresh -- a fixture question, not a wiring one.
